claims.text: On August 5, 2026, the Dow Jones Industrial Average rose by 0.5 percent to achieve its third consecutive record close, while the Nasdaq and S&P 500 finished lower.
Briefing.com analyst Patrick O'Hare stated that stock market investors are largely operating with a bullish mindset on hopes of reopening the Strait of Hormuz.
Iran Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei stated that factors making the Strait of Hormuz insecure still exist due to aggressive actions and a naval blockade by the United States.
SpaceX stock dropped 13.6 percent after reporting quarterly expenditures exceeding $18 billion for the three months ending in June.
Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei announced that Iran and Oman agreed on the geographical coordinates for a shipping route through the Strait of Hormuz.
Iranian Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi stated that the proposed shipping route through the Strait of Hormuz is temporary and could remain open for two to four months.
Approximately one-fifth of the world's oil and liquefied natural gas exports normally pass through the Strait of Hormuz.
In June, Iran and the United States signed a Memorandum of Understanding to end hostilities and reopen the Strait of Hormuz within 60 days, but the agreement collapsed shortly after.
Negotiations between Iran and Oman involve a draft agreement that would place inbound commercial shipping through the Strait of Hormuz under Iranian control.
Kazem Gharibabadi stated that the planned shipping route will pass through both Iranian and Omani territorial waters.
US Central Command reported that its forces redirected 48 commercial vessels, disabled two, and boarded two as part of its naval blockade against Iran.
Yemen's Houthi rebels launched missile strikes against the Saudi Arabian oil tanker Wafa off the coast of Yanbu in the Red Sea and targeted the oil tanker Daisy in the Gulf of Aden.
Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei became Iran's supreme leader after replacing his father, Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, who was killed in initial strikes by the US and Israel on February 28.
Russian missile and drone strikes on the Kyiv region injured over 40 people and started fires in multiple locations.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy stated that additional US-made Patriot interceptors are needed to protect Ukrainian civilians from Russian strikes.
Peter Zalmayev, director of the Eurasia Democracy Initiative, described the Russia-Ukraine war as having entered an escalatory spiral of attrition.
Russian forces launched 115 drones and 24 ballistic missiles across Ukraine, killing 21 people.
Ukraine intercepted many incoming Russian drones, but depleted air defenses failed to stop several ballistic missiles from hitting targets near Kyiv.
A surge in reciprocal drone and missile strikes between Russia and Ukraine caused civilian fatalities on both sides amid stalled diplomatic negotiations.
Abdul El-Sayed won the Democratic primary for Michigan's US Senate seat, defeating Representative Haley Stevens.
Abdul El-Sayed defeated Haley Stevens in the Democratic primary by a vote margin of 48.5 percent to 47.5 percent.
The United Democracy Project, a Super PAC connected to AIPAC, spent more than $30 million supporting Haley Stevens and opposing Abdul El-Sayed in the primary.
Republicans hold a 53 to 47 majority over Democrats in the United States Senate.
State Representative Donavan McKinney defeated incumbent Congressman Shri Thanedar in the Democratic primary for Michigan's 13th Congressional District with 51.9 percent of the vote.
Donavan McKinney was endorsed by Senator Bernie Sanders, Representative Rashida Tlaib, and the Justice Democrats.
In Missouri's Democratic primary, Wesley Bell defeated former congresswoman Cori Bush.
William Lawrence won a Democratic primary for a US House seat in Michigan after campaigning to stop US arms sales to Israel.
Former Bangladesh Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina announced during a virtual press conference in New Delhi that she plans to return to Bangladesh in December.
The Foreign Ministry of Bangladesh expressed outrage over India allowing Sheikh Hasina to address the media, describing her as an absconding convicted genocider.
Sheikh Hasina was sentenced to death in absentia by a tribunal in Dhaka in 2025 for alleged crimes against humanity.
According to the United Nations, nearly 1,400 people were killed in Bangladesh during the youth-led uprising in 2024 that led to Sheikh Hasina's departure.
Tarique Rahman became Prime Minister of Bangladesh after the Bangladesh Nationalist Party won elections held in February.
Prosecutors in Dhaka used a verified audio recording of Sheikh Hasina authorizing deadly force against protesters as evidence in her conviction.
Sheikh Hasina stated that her decision to return to Bangladesh is aimed at restoring democracy, human rights, and political stability rather than seeking power.
German authorities launched a counterterrorism investigation after an explosive-laden drone was discovered near Ukrainian Antonov cargo planes at Leipzig/Halle Airport.
A DHL cargo plane collided in mid-air with an unknown object after aborting its landing at Leipzig/Halle Airport, sustaining minor damage before landing safely in Hanover.
German Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt stated that the Leipzig drone incident is being treated as part of a professional hybrid threat scenario.
German police deployed a bomb disposal robot to remove the detonator from the drone found at Leipzig/Halle Airport before performing a controlled explosion.
Leipzig/Halle Airport serves as an operational base for Ukraine's Antonov Airlines and is used by NATO and the German military for logistics.
Ukrainian Ambassador to Germany Oleksii Makeiev accused Russia of being behind the explosive drone found at Leipzig/Halle Airport.
German police discovered up to 800 grams of plastic explosive, containing PETN and semtex, attached to the drone at Leipzig airport.
A 2024 pan-European investigation identified 22 suspects in Poland and Lithuania linked to Russian intelligence over parcel firebombs sent via DHL.
An Israeli airstrike on a cemetery prayer hall in Tibnin, Lebanon, killed one person and wounded 12 others.
The Israeli military issued an evacuation warning for the town of Mansouri, its first displacement order in southern Lebanon since June 14.
Lebanon's Health Ministry reported that Israeli military attacks have killed at least 4,333 people in Lebanon since March 2.
Two Israeli soldiers were killed and several others injured when an improvised explosive device detonated inside a booby-trapped building in Majdal Selem, southern Lebanon.
Hezbollah leader Naim Qassem criticized US-sponsored peace talks in Rome between Israel and Lebanon, claiming they bring nothing but shame and humiliation.
The June framework deal sponsored by the US includes Hezbollah's disarmament, the phased withdrawal of Israeli forces, and the deployment of the Lebanese army into southern pilot zones.
Italian Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani spoke with his Iranian counterpart to urge Tehran to halt Hezbollah's military operations.
Meta's Chief Global Affairs Officer Joel Kaplan apologized to Indian IT Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw for a platform error that restricted a video posted by Prime Minister Narendra Modi.

Indian parliamentary committee chief Nishikant Dubey gave Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg a three-day deadline to apologize for removing Prime Minister Modi's post or face the loss of legal safe harbour protection.
Meta representatives admitted to Indian officials that the platform accepted money to boost specific categories of content, including illegal material.
Section 79 of India's Information Technology Act grants legal immunity to online intermediaries from liability for user-generated content under specific conditions.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi's video post addressing students about exam paper leaks was restricted on Facebook for five hours on July 28.
Indian authorities issued notices to Meta regarding a BBC Eye investigation that documented advertisements promoting child sexual abuse material on Instagram.
Activist Sonam Wangchuk completed a 26-day hunger strike in New Delhi to demand reforms to India's examination and education systems.
Graduate unemployment in India has remained between 35 percent and 40 percent over the past 25 years.
Dharmendra Pradhan resigned as India's Education Minister on July 25 following widespread student protests.
Opposition leader Rahul Gandhi held a press conference accusing Home Minister Amit Shah of ordering police violence against student protesters in Delhi on July 20.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi released a video stating he wished to forgive student protesters who used offensive language against him during demonstrations.
The Cockroach Janta Party conducted a 36-day protest movement using social media memes and satirical content to highlight student grievances.
Cockroach Janta Party founder Abhijeet Dipke announced that the organization will operate as an independent pressure group rather than contest political elections.
The Rajya Sabha passed the Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Amendment Bill, 2026, increasing the sanctioned number of Supreme Court judges from 34 to 38.
Union Law Minister Arjun Ram Meghwal stated that expanding the Supreme Court bench will speed up case disposal and provide flexibility for Constitution benches.
Opposition lawmakers walked out of the Rajya Sabha in protest prior to the vote on the Supreme Court judge expansion bill.
Congress MP Vivek Tankha stated during the Rajya Sabha debate that approximately 95,000 cases are currently pending before the Supreme Court.
Trinamool Congress MP Menaka Guruswamy stated that female judges represent only 14 percent of all High Court judges in India.
The Indian government proposed a three-day special parliamentary session from August 16 to August 18 to debate the Delimitation Bill.
The Lok Sabha passed the Bankers' Books Evidence Bill, 2026, introduced by Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman.
The proposed Delimitation Bill aims to expand the number of seats in the Lok Sabha by over 50 percent and reserve one-third of seats for women starting in 2029.
